methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $1.0B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Waabi, a Series C autonomous transportation company founded by Raquel Urtasun, operates within a frontier-tech transportation sector characterized by eight identifiable private peers including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, and ZeroAvia. No direct public comparables exist in this segment. The target has raised $1.0B to date.

Valuation analysis employed stage-progression methodology, the only applicable triangulation approach given insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage peer density. Using total capital raised as a proxy base and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C progression yielded an implied valuation of $1.7B. Peer-median analysis was not viable; while three same-sector companies exist, none satisfied minimum thresholds (≥3 datapoints) across same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier filters necessary for meaningful median extraction. Reliance on all-sector medians was rejected as methodologically unsound given sector heterogeneity.

The triangulated range supports a median valuation of $1.7B, with a plausible band of $1.4B to $2.0B reflecting uncertainty bounds around stage-progression step-up calibration. Key valuation sensitivities include: the applicability of 1.7x multiplier assumptions derived from broader venture data; absence of direct peer benchmarking in autonomous transportation; and limited visibility into unit economics or path-to-profitability metrics. Resolution of these uncertainties—particularly through identification of comparable Series C-stage transportation exits or contemporaneous fundings—would materially refine this range.
